messages:
ella: Quick help please  we're evaluating TwinLedger and ParseLine for invoice automation. Their proposals arrived and the pricing models are totally different. anyone have quick experience?
sam: I did a short POC with ParseLine last year. Good extractor, flexible mappings. Pricing: they did a hybrid: per-invoice + per-line-item for some line types. can share notes.
ravi: TwinLedger? heard good things about throughput but not pricing specifics.
ella: Vendor excerpts pasted below from the proposals: 
```
TwinLedger (Enterprise): $0.035 per invoice processed, tiered to $0.03 @ >200k/mo. Line-item extraction included up to 10 lines/invoice; additional lines $0.0008/line. Attachment handling: $0.006/page unless uploaded via S3 ingestion (waived). Min annual commit: $60k. Includes SSO & API.
ParseLine (Enterprise): $0.05 per invoice + $0.0025 per extracted field. PDFs billed at $0.009/page. POC: 45 days sandbox. Min commit: $35k. GL mapping exports billed as PS unless included in enterprise pack.
```
sam: That's classic. ParseLine's per-field will be unpredictable for us (many nested line items). TwinLedger's approach seems more predictable but they sneak in line caps.
biz-ops: Key requirements from finance: 1) line-item-level output with tax/discount breakouts; 2) programmatic export (S3 + webhook) and a reconciled payload schema; 3) audit log retention 7 yrs and SIEM-forwardable logs; 4) DPA + KMS/HSM support and list of subprocessors; 5) processing SLA: nightly batches <3h, ad-hoc <30m for critical.
ella: Procurement asked me to confirm three things before replying: how each vendor counts line-items/fields, sample cost at our projected volume (1.2M invoices/yr) including worst-case line counts, and whether GL mapping rules are exportable/versionable.
ravi: Add: ask for their acceptance test methodology and whether we can run accuracy benchmarks on our dataset in sandbox, and if they will provide credits if accuracy < agreed benchmark after onboarding.
ella: Draft question list I'm planning to send  please quick edit: 
1) Can you ingest our BigQuery export + GCS attachments (we'll share schema)? Any schema gaps?
2) Exact pricing formula: how do you count invoices vs pages vs fields vs line items? Provide formula and examples.
3) Provide a sample cost spreadsheet showing monthly charges at 50k / 150k / 300k invoice tiers for 12/24 month terms, with best/worst-case line counts.
4) Do you include line-item extraction (tax/discounts/FX) in the per-invoice price or bill separately? If separate, provide per-line fees.
5) Do you waive per-page attachment fees for S3 ingested attachments or pre-processed OCR payloads?
6) Is SSO (SAML + SCIM) included in enterprise or extra? Is SCIM provisioning supported?
7) Can GL mappings and reconciliation rules be exported as YAML/JSON and stored in our repo? Is there versioning and rollback?
8) Do you provide webhooks + S3 dump for reconciled payloads and audit logs in a format we can forward to Splunk?
9) SLA language for processing latency and accuracy targets; do you provide credits/remedies for missed SLAs or acceptance failures?
10) Will you sign our DPA and support KMS/HSM controls and disclose subprocessors?
11) Typical onboarding PS hours included vs billable. Can you commit X hours in year 1 as part of the package?
12) Do you offer a 30-day escape clause in year 1 if the sandbox acceptance accuracy is below agreed benchmark?

sam: I'd also ask them to show a sample mapped payload for one of our typical vendor invoices (we can redact). ask for a CSV of line counts distribution so we can model costs.
ravi: negotiation levers to consider: lower per-invoice at scale, cap effective per-invoice rate (e.g., don't charge > $0.04 effective even with line fees), include onboarding hours and connector builds in commit, waive per-page if attachments come via our pipeline, and a credit schedule tied to acceptance tests.
procurement-bot: Reminder: attach the RFP, sample BigQuery export, and cost model template. Use /procure/reply-template-v5.
biz-ops: Two hard stop items: must export mapping rules (no vendor-locked rules) and must provide audit logs acceptable for Splunk ingestion. If vendor refuses either, pass.
ella: i'll send these questions to both vendors and paste replies here. if they push field-level pricing hard, we'll ask for a firm cap and sample worst-case invoice invoice. thanks all :thumbsup:
